# Keyword reference

How each Abaqus keyword is handled. The converter knows the complete CalculiX 2.22 + 2.23 keyword set (**143** cards). Anything in that set is emitted as-is; anything outside it without a translator is commented out with guidance — never silently dropped.

## Translated / converted to an equivalent

| Abaqus keyword | Handling |
| --- | --- |
| `*NODE / *ELEMENT / *NSET / *ELSET` | parsed into the geometry registry and re-emitted canonically (sets resolved, `GEN`→`GENERATE`, gappy ranges pruned). `*NODE, SYSTEM=C` / `S` coordinates (R, θ, Z / R, θ, φ, angles in degrees, φ up from the X-Y plane) are converted to Cartesian, and so is a normal on such a line (Abaqus reads it in the same form); a shell normal given on the node (fields 5-7) becomes a `*NORMAL` line for each shell element there, as Abaqus uses it (ccx would average the element normals); on beam nodes it is dropped (reduced physics). A truss numbered below the beams at a node they share ends at a tied copy of the node, which gets a knot beam (ccx would give the node no rotations); a truss at a shell node without a beam ends at a copy tied to the node through a hub of two knot beams (ccx's own knot there can be singular: a crash without a message). |
| `*NGEN / *NFILL / *NCOPY / *ELGEN / *ELCOPY` | expanded into explicit `*NODE`/`*ELEMENT` (CalculiX has no mesh-generation cards); an `*NFILL` set holds its bounding nodes too, as in Abaqus. `*NMAP` maps the coordinates (`RECTANGULAR`, `CYLINDRICAL`, `SPHERICAL`, `ROTATION`, `TRANSLATION`, `SCALE`; `*NODE` normals turn with the local axes); `DIAMOND`, `TOROIDAL`, `BLENDED` are not converted (reduced physics). |
| `*PART / *INSTANCE / *ASSEMBLY` | flattened into one global numbering (instance transform applied, references resolved, names kept ≤80 chars); part-level constraints (`*EQUATION`, `*MPC`, `*RIGID BODY`, `*COUPLING`, `*DISTRIBUTING COUPLING`, `*PRE-TENSION SECTION`, ...) copied per instance, also from inside an `*INSTANCE` (another card there is left out, warned); a part's `*DISTRIBUTION` gets per-instance names (also where an `*ORIENTATION` or a composite ply names it) and offset element labels; a part's `*ORIENTATION, DEFINITION=NODES` names each instance's own nodes; rotated instances rotate `*ORIENTATION` axes (also per-element `*DISTRIBUTION` axes), beam `n1`, `*NODE` normals, `*NORMAL` vectors and the part's DOF-numbered data (`*EQUATION` terms, couplings of some DOFs, `SPRING1`/`SPRING2`/`DASHPOT1` DOFs, `*GAP` directions, a hinge's axis, an anisotropic `*MASS`'s axes). Proved by `validate_with_ccx.py` (`assembly_rotated_instances`: the same results as the model written flat). |
| `*ORIENTATION` | origin `c` of a 9-value line subtracted from `a`, `b` (ccx has no origin field); `DEFINITION=NODES` resolved to coordinates, `OFFSET TO NODES` commented; `SPHERICAL`→`RECTANGULAR` and a cylindrical system's rotation line dropped (ccx has neither; warned, a note where every section that reads the orientation gets Abaqus' directions per element or has an isotropic material, a spherical one then written as the global axes); a rectangular one's rotation line kept (a blank axis as 1, Abaqus' default). One that names a `*DISTRIBUTION` is preceded by that distribution in ccx's form (see `*DISTRIBUTION`). Sections and plies of a `*DEFORMATION PLASTICITY` material name none: ccx 2.23's results depend on the axes (CalculiX issue #160), Abaqus' do not. |
| `*DISTRIBUTION` | per-element orientations, in the form ccx 2.23 runs correctly: each `*ORIENTATION` naming one gets its own copy (ccx gives a distribution to the first only), resolved to one line per element of its solid sections — default line first, origin subtracted, the additional rotation applied to the axes (ccx turns only the first line), a name ccx would read as a number replaced; its shell and membrane sections are split into one plain `*ORIENTATION` + section per direction (ccx gives a shell section the first line). A distribution no `*ORIENTATION` names (shell thickness, material property) is commented. |
| `*DISTRIBUTION TABLE` | dropped for an orientation distribution (ccx needs no table; its lines are always `a, b`); otherwise commented. |
| `*SOLID SECTION` | keeps `ELSET`/`MATERIAL`/`ORIENTATION`; other params dropped; an undefined `MATERIAL` is warned (ccx 2.23 segfaults on it where the section is the deck's last card). On `CPS4I`/`CPE4I` elements written as `C3D8I` slabs: no thickness line (it is the slab's depth), and plane stress through a generated `<material>_PLANE_STRESS` `ORTHO` material (see the element reference). |
| `*SECTION CONTROLS` | no ccx card (ccx's elements have their own, fixed formulation): commented out. A note where no option it sets applies to the elements of the sections naming it (Abaqus 2017 Keywords Guide: hourglass options act on first-order reduced-integration and modified elements, element deletion / degradation / viscosity on progressive damage, `SECOND ORDER ACCURACY`, `KINEMATIC SPLIT`, `DISTORTION CONTROL` and the like only in Abaqus/Explicit; the default `HOURGLASS` — `STIFFNESS` in Abaqus/Standard, `ENHANCED` on hyperelastic materials and modified elements — changes nothing; data-line factors of 1 are the defaults, and the out-of-plane, bulk-viscosity and drill factors act only in Abaqus/Explicit); otherwise a warning and reduced physics. |
| `*SHELL SECTION` | thickness only (integration-point count dropped); composite plies → one synthesized `*ORIENTATION` per ply angle, composed with a base rotation about the normal, every ply naming one where any does (ccx 2.23 gives a ply without one the previous ply's); where ccx would place the material directions of an orthotropic or anisotropic section otherwise than Abaqus (another plane, a rotation about axis 1 or 2, a curved shell, a `*DISTRIBUTION` whose axis 3 is not the normal) each element group gets Abaqus' directions, plies included, as `*ORIENTATION`s in the shell's plane; composite S3/S4/S4R elements become S6/S8R (ccx runs composites on those only); `SYMMETRIC` layups mirrored; on continuum shells (SC6R/SC8R, which run as solids) → `*SOLID SECTION`, with Abaqus' material directions per element (a `*DISTRIBUTION`) where ccx's solid would take an orthotropic or anisotropic section's axes unprojected, a composite one → one `*SOLID SECTION` per ply material and angle on one solid per ply (up to `--max-ply-elements`); with a `*DISTRIBUTION` orientation (its own or a ply's) split into one element set, plain `*ORIENTATION` and section per distinct direction. `OFFSET=SPOS`/`SNEG` → `0.5`/`-0.5` (ccx takes only the number and reads it the same way). |
| `*SHELL GENERAL SECTION` | → `*SHELL SECTION` (thickness+material form); ABD/stiffness form flagged as unsupported. |
| `*MEMBRANE SECTION` | passed through; material directions as for `*SHELL SECTION` (ccx 2.23 takes a membrane's orientation axes unprojected, the global axes without one, so an orthotropic or anisotropic membrane off them gets Abaqus' directions per element group); with a `*DISTRIBUTION` orientation split into one element set, plain `*ORIENTATION` and section per distinct direction. On quadratic membranes (`M3D6`, `M3D8`, `M3D8R`, `M3D9`, `M3D9R`), which become solids, → `*SOLID SECTION` (split off where linear membranes share it); the thickness (data line, `NODAL THICKNESS`, `MEMBRANE THICKNESS`) goes into their geometry. ccx has no `DENSITY` (mass per area added to the material's) or `POISSON` (Abaqus' thickness change under `NLGEOM`): where mass acts, `DENSITY` goes into a copy of the material with `DENSITY` / thickness more (a varying thickness: warned, reduced physics); `POISSON` (default 0.5; `MATERIAL`, Abaqus/Explicit's default, as ccx) is warned under `NLGEOM` where it differs from the ratio ccx's membranes thin with, their material's (elastic: its own; 0.5 with plasticity). |
| `*BEAM SECTION` | keeps the supported params; `SECTION=CIRC`: the Abaqus radius becomes ccx's two section diameters (`r` → `2r, 2r`), and 2-node beams under it become 3-node beams with an inserted midside node (ccx 2.23 rejects linear beams with a circular section). `SECTION=PIPE` (outer radius, wall thickness) and `BOX` (`a, b, t1..t4`) data pass through, as both codes read them alike, and `THICK PIPE` → `PIPE`; ccx 2.23 runs these sections only on `B32R`, so their beams become `B32R` (2-node ones with an inserted midside node; see the element reference). `SECTION=I` (a T with one flange zero), `HEX`, `TRAPEZOID` and `ARBITRARY` with the node at the centroid run as ccx's `U1` beam where the deck allows it (see `*BEAM GENERAL SECTION`), with the properties Abaqus gives them. Otherwise they are commented out, and under `--approximate` `SECTION=I` becomes the `RECT` of equal area and strong-axis inertia. |
| `*BEAM GENERAL SECTION` | a `RECT`, `CIRC`, `PIPE` or `BOX` profile → ccx's `*BEAM SECTION` of that profile with a material from E and G (ν = E / 2G − 1; 0 in a 2-D model, where Abaqus does not use G), the density and the thermal expansion (`SECT=` read as `SECTION=`). `SECTION=GENERAL` (A, I11, I12, I22, J; n1; E, G) and the `I` (or T), `HEX`, `TRAPEZOID` and `ARBITRARY` profiles → ccx 2.23's 2-node beam `U1` (`*USER ELEMENT`, `*BEAM SECTION, SECTION=GENERAL`) with a material from E, G and `DENSITY`: the principal second moments, n1 turned onto the first principal axis and projected normal to each element (one card per direction), a shear area that makes `U1` an Euler–Bernoulli beam (its shear term is wrong in 2.23) and a Poisson's ratio that sets its torsion G (I11 + I22) to G J. `U1` runs only in a linear elastic, isothermal deck without elements ccx expands, constraints on beam nodes, NLGEOM, `*BUCKLE` or `*DYNAMIC`; there, and in space where no Poisson's ratio below 0.5 gives G J, the shear centre lies off the centroid or Abaqus computes J numerically (`TRAPEZOID`, `ARBITRARY`; unless `--approximate`; a 2-D model has no torsion and holds DOFs 3–5), the card is commented out with the reason; an `L` never (its node is at the legs' corner). Line loads and gravity on `U1` become nodal forces with consistent end moments; RF at `U1` nodes is wrong in ccx 2.23 (warned). `*CENTROID` and `*BEAM SECTION OFFSET` off the axis and `TAPER` keep the beams off `U1`; after a `U1` section `*CENTROID`, `*SHEAR CENTER`, `*TRANSVERSE SHEAR STIFFNESS` and `*SECTION POINTS` are commented out with a note. |
| `*LOAD CASE` | in a linear perturbation `*STATIC` or `*STEADY STATE DYNAMICS` step: one ccx step per load case, holding the step's cards outside the blocks and the case's own, each about the base state (a `*BOUNDARY, OP=NEW` anywhere releases the base-state BCs in every case, as in Abaqus); elsewhere, where Abaqus rejects it, the cases are superposed, warned. |
| `*STEP` | `NAME` dropped; `NLGEOM`, `INC`, `AMPLITUDE=RAMP/STEP` kept (dropped on explicit steps, which Abaqus/Explicit runs without it; `NLGEOM=NO` with `*DEFORMATION PLASTICITY`, see there); `PERTURBATION` kept only for `*FREQUENCY`/`*BUCKLE` (warned when steps follow, which start from its deformed state) and written on a `*BUCKLE` step after a general step (Abaqus buckles about the preloaded base state, ccx without it the unloaded structure); on a `*FREQUENCY` step written after an `NLGEOM` general step, or after linear steps that only heat temperature-dependent materials (Abaqus uses the base temperatures, ccx's plain step the initial ones), dropped after other general steps without `NLGEOM`, on a first step with initial stresses and before modal / steady-state dynamics, which refuse perturbation eigenmodes (Abaqus includes the preload's stress stiffness only after `NLGEOM`; warned where not exact); explicit steps get `INC=10000000` + `NLGEOM`, a `*MODAL DYNAMIC` step `INC=` where its period / increment exceeds its `INC` or 100 (Abaqus ignores `INC` there); a step whose displacement BCs get ccx's step ramp (see `*BOUNDARY`) gets `AMPLITUDE=STEP`, ccx's default there; a general step after linear perturbation steps starts with the last general step's loads, BCs, temperatures and `NLGEOM` given again (ccx carries a perturbation step's on); a `*MODAL DYNAMIC` step's loads are its own (`*CLOAD` / `*DLOAD, OP=NEW` first where earlier steps gave such loads, which ccx 2.23 applies there too); `*END STEP` ensured. |
| `*STATIC` | `RIKS` commented out by default, with `*NO ANALYSIS` in its place: ccx stops at that step (it would silently run it as plain static; reduced physics; `--approximate` reframes it); `DIRECT=NO STOP` → `DIRECT`; `STABILIZE` dropped (warned). |
| `*COMPLEX FREQUENCY` | commented out, with `*NO ANALYSIS` in its place: ccx stops at that step (ccx's card computes Coriolis or flutter modes only, without damping; reduced physics). |
| `*DYNAMIC` | implicit and `EXPLICIT` both native; `DIRECT USER CONTROL` → `DIRECT`; `APPLICATION=QUASI-STATIC/MODERATE DISSIPATION` → `ALPHA=-0.3333` (and `*STEP AMPLITUDE=RAMP` for quasi-static); other Abaqus/Explicit controls dropped. An explicit step in a deck with circular-section beams gets a maximum time increment (4th data field): ccx 2.23 overestimates their stable increment about 1.3-fold (NaN displacements); so does one with contact of plane / axisymmetric elements on a rigid surface, which ccx 2.23 leaves out of its stable increment (the contact bounces): ccx's contact formula with the slave nodes' masses, times 0.8. A fixed `DIRECT` increment above a cap is warned. |
| `*FIXED MASS SCALING / *VARIABLE MASS SCALING` | commented out. `FACTOR=f` on the whole model, the same in every explicit step → densities, `*MASS` values and rotary inertias f times larger, specific heats and GRAV magnitudes f times smaller (Abaqus' gravity and thermal response keep the true mass): Abaqus' scaled mass matrix. A target increment `DT` (`TYPE=BELOW MIN`) → with `--approximate` ccx's selective mass scaling (`DT` the step's minimum increment). `FACTOR` on part of the model (`ELSET`, overriding the global one) → per section of one factor a copy of its materials with density × f and specific heat / f, `*MASS` values and rotary inertias × f, GRAV magnitudes / f, on a set per factor where a GRAV set holds several. Otherwise (a section of two factors, a user material, a factor that changes between steps, `DT` on part of the model, `TYPE=UNIFORM` / `SET EQUAL DT` with `DT`, `ROLLING`) a numerical control: ccx runs the true mass. |
| `*FREQUENCY` | Abaqus-only params dropped; `EIGENSOLVER=SUBSPACE` max-frequency field blanked (ccx reads it as the lower bound); `NORMALIZATION=DISPLACEMENT` noted (ccx mass-normalizes). The step's `*CLOAD` / `*DLOAD` / `*DSLOAD` are commented out: Abaqus ignores them. |
| `*BUCKLE` | `EIGENSOLVER` dropped; Abaqus range/size fields blanked where ccx reads accuracy/vectors/iterations. A `*BUCKLE` step, or the step after a `*STEP, PERTURBATION` one, that would hold no body load once an earlier step held one gets a zero `GRAV` line (ccx 2.23 aborts after such a step). Its `*TEMPERATURE`, which ccx refuses there, is commented out: Abaqus scales the change with the factor (thermal buckling), reduced physics. ccx 2.23 does not solve a `*STEP, PERTURBATION` `*BUCKLE` step for prescribed displacements (only those nodes move): there nonzero BCs held on from earlier steps are given again at 0, and a step loaded by its own drops `PERTURBATION` before any general step, else is warned (reduced physics). Loads and BCs on an amplitude are scaled by its value at time 0, which Abaqus applies there (ccx ignores the amplitude). |
| `*HEAT TRANSFER` | `END=` / `MXDEM` dropped. A transient step without `DELTMX` gets `DIRECT`: Abaqus then takes fixed increments of the initial increment, ccx its own. A transient step with temperature DOFs and no initial temperatures starts every node at 0, the Abaqus default (ccx 2.23 stops without them). |
| `*COUPLED TEMPERATURE-DISPLACEMENT` | passed through. ccx 2.23 solves the transient form as a dynamic step (HHT) with the mass of every `*DENSITY` and `*MASS`, where Abaqus/Standard neglects inertia: in such a deck the densities and `*MASS` values are divided by 10³⁰ and the specific heats and GRAV / CENTRIF magnitudes multiplied by it, which leaves the heat capacity (density × specific heat) and the body forces as they were — unless a dynamic or eigenvalue step needs the mass (then warned). A mechanical load that jumps at the start of such a step (no `AMPLITUDE`), or a BC that `*BOUNDARY, OP=NEW` releases there, is warned: ccx's HHT integration overshoots the jump by 5 % at the first increment. |
| `*MASS` | passed through; in a deck with a transient `*COUPLED TEMPERATURE-DISPLACEMENT` step divided by 10³⁰ with the densities (see there), times an explicit `*FIXED MASS SCALING` factor (see there). `TYPE=ANISOTROPIC` (ccx 2.23 has none) → the smallest principal mass on the node, the rest per principal axis on new nodes that `*EQUATION`s tie to it along that axis (exact; reduced physics under `NLGEOM` at a node with rotations, whose axes Abaqus turns, and where the `ORIENTATION`'s axes are unknown: then M11 alone). |
| `*DASHPOT` | of `DASHPOT1` / `DASHPOT2` elements: written without its DOF line, which ccx reads as a coefficient and stops on in a dynamic step, and without `ORIENTATION` (see the elements); of `DASHPOTA` elements without a DOF line where Abaqus has a blank one (ccx stops on `1, 1`). |
| `*SPRING` | numbers written with a decimal point (`100` → `100.`, `1e-3` → `1.e-3`): ccx 2.23 reads a line without one as the DOF line and stops; a `SPRINGA` card's DOF line (Abaqus: blank) left out. `SPRING1` / `SPRING2` DOFs at a node with a `*TRANSFORM` are Abaqus' local ones, ccx springs the global DOF → the spring on a new node tied to the local DOF (exact). |
| `*BOUNDARY` | named types (`ENCASTRE`/`PINNED`/`*SYMM`) expanded to DOFs; `TYPE=VELOCITY`/`ACCELERATION` → a displacement BC whose generated amplitude integrates the history from the DOF's state at the step start (continued in later steps that keep it). Without `AMPLITUDE` a displacement (DOFs 1-6) follows Abaqus, not the procedure's default: Abaqus/Standard always ramps it from its value at the end of the previous step, so where ccx would step it (implicit `*DYNAMIC`, `*VISCO`, transient (un)coupled steps, `*STEP, AMPLITUDE=STEP`) the line gets ccx's own step ramp (`AMPLITUDE=RAMP12357111317`; on a node with a `*TRANSFORM` only where that ramp starts from the DOF's value, else at once, warned); Abaqus/Explicit ignores the value and holds the DOF where it is (a zero BC, or `FIXED` where the DOF may have moved; a rotation or a node with a `*TRANSFORM` it cannot hold is kept, warned). Zero lines on DOFs still at zero stay as they are. DOFs 4-6 dropped on nodes of plane/axisymmetric or truss elements (no rotations there, Abaqus ignores them; ccx stops on them at truss nodes, and 2.23 builds without a fix crash at plane ones), and DOFs 7 (warping) and 9 (electric potential), which ccx does not have, where no element of the model has them; DOF 8 (pore, fluid or acoustic pressure), which ccx reads as the rotation about x, where no element of the converted model has it: pore-pressure elements lose it with their `P` suffix, a `*FLUID CAVITY` reference node with the card (both warned; a prescribed cavity pressure is a load the converted deck lacks). `LOAD CASE` dropped (Abaqus reads it only in `*BUCKLE`); in steady-state dynamics `IMAGINARY` (the out-of-phase part, also on `*CLOAD`, `*DLOAD` and `*DSLOAD`) → ccx's `LOAD CASE=2`; in a `*BUCKLE` step the `LOAD CASE=2` cards that repeat `LOAD CASE=1` cards (the Abaqus/CAE default) are left out, and differing buckling-mode BCs are left out as reduced physics (ccx has one set of BCs per step). An element end node of a circular-section beam whose rotational BCs hold only some of DOFs 4-6, or a nonzero one, gets a force-free knot beam (elset/material `ABQ2CCX_KNOT`): ccx 2.23 would lock the node's other rotations too. A later step's `OP=NEW`, once shell/beam nodes have had rotational BCs, is dropped when the step re-specifies every BC; where it removes BCs, the shell/beam nodes whose rotations it would break get knot beams too (ccx 2.23 does not rebuild those rotations after `OP=NEW`). An `OP=NEW` on a later card of a step whose first card has none is dropped, warned (ccx 2.23 acts on it on a step's first `*BOUNDARY` only; Abaqus requires it on all of them). On a DOF a rigid constraint also eliminates (ccx stops: dependent side of a MPC and a SPC) the BC is taken off where the reference node's own BCs impose it; identical ones on a `*RIGID BODY` move to its reference node with zero rotations about the other axes, as Abaqus/Standard moves them, where the BC'd nodes hold the same DOFs; the rest is warned (`--approximate` drops it on a kinematic coupling or an `*MPC` and makes the `*RIGID BODY` move, as Abaqus/Standard does). Two rotations held on a shell node that is no knot, about axes off its normal: one rotation line where the free axis lies in the shell plane (ccx 2.23 holds both in-plane rotations for two), else warned. Rotations of a node with a `*TRANSFORM`: see `*TRANSFORM`. `USER` (Abaqus `DISP`) commented, naming ccx's `uboun.f`. |
| `*DLOAD` | pressures and body loads passed through (`Px` faces match Abaqus); `P` on shells kept and on membranes written `P1` (both push along the element normal in Abaqus and ccx; ccx stops on `P` on a membrane), split between the faces of ccx's expanded element as for `*DSLOAD`; bare `P` on solids flagged; `P1`..`P4` on `CPS4I`/`CPE4I` slabs → `P3`..`P6`; a pressure on `CAX8R` / `CAX6` edges whose midside node lies off the middle or off the chord → consistent nodal forces in a deck without NLGEOM (ccx 2.23 integrates it at 2 points along the edge, Abaqus fully; under NLGEOM kept, warned); a line without an element set (Abaqus: the whole model) gets a whole-model set; `FOLLOWER=NO` / `CONSTANT RESULTANT` dropped (warned under NLGEOM on edge loads; Abaqus reads them for tractions and edge loads only). Element tractions (`TRVECn`/`TRSHRn`) and beam line loads (`PX`/`PY`/`PZ`/`P1`/`P2` — ccx reads `P1`/`P2` on a beam as a section-face pressure) → consistent nodal forces, as for `*DSLOAD` tractions, and so do `TRVEC`/`TRSHR`/`P` on surface elements (which leave the mesh; `P` is positive along the element normal); gravity on them adds nothing (no mass), other loads on them are commented; user-subroutine labels (`...NU`) commented, naming ccx's `dload.f`. A `P` on rigid elements → a face pressure on their skins (minus p on the `SPOS` skin's face: Abaqus' P pushes along the element normal; on R2D2 / RB2D2, which have no section thickness, per unit depth); gravity on rigid elements alone applies nothing (they carry no mass), a body force per volume on them is commented. `BX` / `BY` / `BZ` on shells (a body force per unit volume; ccx applies it as a face pressure there) → `GRAV` of B / density along the axis on a set of the shells of their own (`ABQ2CCX_BODY_…`), or consistent nodal forces of B times the thickness where the material has no single constant density. `OP=NEW` keeps the `*DSLOAD` pressures Abaqus keeps (ccx's `OP=NEW` would remove them) and removes the earlier `BX` / `BY` / `BZ` with zero lines (ccx's keeps them). A load on faces that a later step loads from another surface, set or card is given again in that step (Abaqus adds the two, ccx keeps one value per face; on another amplitude or a step-time one, warned). GRAV and CENTRIF magnitudes are multiplied by 10³⁰ where the masses are divided by it (see `*COUPLED TEMPERATURE-DISPLACEMENT`). |
| `*DSLOAD` | surface pressure → `*DLOAD` with `Px` face labels (on the `SPOS` / `SNEG` side of rigid elements: their skins' face; on `CAX8R` / `CAX6` edges as for `*DLOAD`); on a shell's / membrane's `SNEG` side → `P` / `P1`, on its `SPOS` side the same with the sign flipped (Abaqus pushes a surface pressure against the surface normal, ccx's `P` / `P1` pushes along the element normal; `validate_with_ccx.py shell_pressure_sides`) — 0.5 − o of it on the expanded element's bottom face, 0.5 + o on its top face (a surface `ABQ2CCX_TOP_…`, `S2`; o the `OFFSET`), since ccx loads a shell's bottom face only, whose area is off the reference surface's by O(t/R) (`validate_with_ccx.py sheet_pressure_*`); surface tractions (`TRVEC`/`TRSHR`, which ccx has no card for) → consistent nodal forces: the face/edge shape functions integrated by Gauss quadrature over the undeformed geometry (times the plane-section thickness, or 2πr on axisymmetric edges; directions normalized and `TRSHR` projected onto the face, as in Abaqus), emitted as a `*CLOAD` (one per amplitude, never `OP=NEW`) at the end of the step. Exact in small-strain steps and, under NLGEOM, for `TRVEC` with `FOLLOWER=NO, CONSTANT RESULTANT=YES`; an NLGEOM follower `TRVEC` / `TRVECn` (`FOLLOWER=YES, CONSTANT RESULTANT=NO`) normal to flat continuum faces → a face pressure, as Abaqus applies its normal part (`validate_with_ccx.py follower_traction_turning`); any other NLGEOM traction is commented (`--approximate` converts it with an `[APPROX]` warning). A pressure on the `SPOS`/`SNEG` side of surface elements (which leave the mesh) → nodal forces too, positive against the surface normal (`SPOS`: the element normal); under NLGEOM only with `--approximate`. On a node with a `*TRANSFORM` the converted forces (also `*DLOAD`'s) are given in its local axes, as ccx and Abaqus read a `*CLOAD` there; a node whose axes are unknown (on the cylinder or polar axis, degenerate, two transforms, a 2-D node turned out of plane) leaves the line commented. |
| `*SURFACE SECTION` | dropped with its surface elements (`SFM3D*`, `SFMAX*`, `SFMGAX*`), which leave the mesh — no stiffness, no ccx element — while their loads become nodal forces; they stay (and ccx stops on them) if `*REBAR LAYER` or `DENSITY=` in a dynamic/frequency step or under gravity gives them physics, unless `--approximate`. |
| `*COHESIVE SECTION / *GASKET SECTION` | → `*SOLID SECTION` (`ELSET`, `MATERIAL`, `ORIENTATION` kept): ccx has no cohesive or gasket element, so they run as thin continuum elements without the traction-separation / closure law (reduced physics). |
| `*TIE` | Abaqus-only params (`TYPE=`) stripped; `ADJUST`/`POSITION TOLERANCE` kept. A line whose master is a rigid surface (rigid elements' skins, a meshed analytical surface) is not written: the slave nodes Abaqus ties — `TIED NSET`, or those within the position tolerance, by default 10 % (surface-to-surface) or 5 % (node-to-surface: `TYPE=NODE TO SURFACE`, Abaqus/Explicit, a node-based slave) of the typical master facet diagonal (an analytical master: the slave facets'), measured from a slave shell's side towards the master unless `NO THICKNESS` — join that rigid body (`NO ROTATION`: translations only), moved to touch the surface unless `ADJUST=NO` — exact, where ccx's tie follows an `NLGEOM` rotation of the body only linearly and stops explicit dynamics. A slave surface on membranes → a node surface of their nodes, which Abaqus ties (ccx would tie its expanded membrane's face, whose bottom nodes its hinge eliminates: `SNEG` ties nothing, `SPOS` a face that shears through the thickness), with Abaqus' position tolerance written out (given, or its default; ccx's own is some 20 times smaller), which a `*TIE` measures from the membrane nodes as ccx does (a tied pair adds the half thickness, also onto a rigid surface); nodes of the master face stay out. One `*TIE` per data line: ccx reads only a card's first. |
| `*MPC` | line by line: `PIN` → `*EQUATION` on DOFs 1-3; `TIE` → per-DOF `*EQUATION` (shell/beam rotations through knots, DOF 11 in thermal steps); `BEAM` → one `*RIGID BODY` per independent node (chained lines one body); `LINK` → linearised `*EQUATION` without `NLGEOM`, ccx `*MPC BEAM` with it (not on beam/shell/plane nodes); `PLANE`/`STRAIGHT` kept; user MPCs and other types commented, line by line. On a node with a `*TRANSFORM` the equations are in its local DOFs, one local term per node (through an untransformed twin node where it would need several); a node without defined local axes, or a `TIE` on a transformed shell/beam node's rotations, leaves its node pair commented. |
| `*CONNECTOR SECTION` | its `CONN3D2`/`CONN2D2` elements (never emitted; ccx has no connector element) become the kinematic constraint of the connection type: `JOIN`, `REVOLUTE`, `ALIGN`, `HINGE` → `*EQUATION`s in the translations and rotation vectors (rotations on a `ROT NODE` or a knot), `*BOUNDARY` lines to ground or a held node (repeated after `OP=NEW`); `BEAM`, `WELD` → `*RIGID BODY` (with the `*MPC BEAM` bodies); `LINK` → as `*MPC LINK`; unconstrained types left out. Under `NLGEOM` only the forms that stay exact (`--approximate`: the rest written linear, `[APPROX]`); a behaviour, other types and explicit-dynamics rotations on beam/shell nodes are commented out with the reason. On a node with a `*TRANSFORM` the rows are in its local DOFs, as ccx reads them (a rotation on its `ROT NODE`, which gets the node's axes; a transformed kinematic reference node's coupling becomes a `*RIGID BODY` for it); commented out where those axes are undefined or a rotation lives on DOFs 4-6 of a transformed shell/beam node, or of a kinematic reference node whose coupling stays a coupling (ccx misreads them). |
| `*EQUATION` | set-name terms resolved to node numbers, multi-node sets paired in sorted order (as Abaqus does unless `UNSORTED`); terms reordered so the eliminated (first) DOF has no BC and is not eliminated elsewhere; an equation that follows from the others and zero BCs (a duplicate, a loop's closing tie) dropped. A term on DOFs 4-6 of a rigid-body reference point → its `ROT NODE`'s DOFs 1-3 (ccx ignores DOFs 4-6 of the REF NODE); an equation with a term on DOFs 4-6 of any other node with a `*TRANSFORM` is commented out (ccx 2.23 misreads such terms). Each equation of a card is resolved on its own. |
| `*KINEMATIC COUPLING` | node-surface `*COUPLING` + `*KINEMATIC` per set of coupled DOFs, a member's lines joined (ccx 2.23 exits on two couplings of one node; the reference node's DOFs 4-6 then take BCs and moments natively); rotation lines on shell/beam nodes become `*EQUATION` ties (see `*COUPLING / *KINEMATIC`), on other nodes they are dropped (reduced physics). |
| `*COUPLING / *KINEMATIC` | `REF NODE` set → node number; empty `*KINEMATIC` (Abaqus: all DOFs) → `1, 3`, which moves the nodes rigidly with the reference node's translations and rotations (`validate_with_ccx.py kinematic_all_dofs`: the same as `*RIGID BODY`); a rotations-only card couples nothing (reduced physics); DOFs > 3 clamped; on 2-D nodes `1, 2` (ccx holds their DOF 3 itself). Shell/membrane/beam/truss nodes get a force-free knot beam (elset/material `ABQ2CCX_KNOT`), without which ccx 2.23 rejects the rigid MPC, and the coupled rotations are tied to the reference node's DOFs 4-6 by `*EQUATION`; a shell/beam `REF NODE` turns the coupling into a `*RIGID BODY` whose `ROT NODE` follows it. A coupling of all translations whose `REF NODE` has a `*TRANSFORM` and a rotation the deck uses (rotational BCs other than all three held at zero, moments, `*EQUATION` terms, connectors) becomes a `*RIGID BODY` whose `ROT NODE` has the node's local axes (ccx's coupling would read them about the global ones). An element surface on membranes, shells or plane / axisymmetric elements → a node surface of their nodes (a plane element's face: its edge's), which Abaqus couples (ccx would couple the expanded faces: 1.2 % off on `M3D4`, a crash on `M3D3` and on knotted shells, other nodes on plane elements: -56 % on `CPE4`); a `*DISTRIBUTING` one becomes equations on the membrane nodes (ccx's card spreads it over faces their hinge holds: about 2 % off, nothing on `M3D3`). |
| `*COUPLING / *DISTRIBUTING` | Abaqus' distributing constraint as `*EQUATION`s (ccx's card only spreads the reference node's loads: a BC there moved nothing, the node printed U = 0): the node moves with the coupling nodes' weighted mean motion plus the rotation of their weighted least-squares fit, and turns with it (a `ROT NODE`, or a shell/beam node's own rotations); weights from tributary areas, a node surface's areas, `WEIGHTING METHOD` and an `INFLUENCE RADIUS` (axisymmetric faces: areas of revolution, as Abaqus' verification decks place the reference node). Kept as ccx's card (warned) under NLGEOM where the equations turn, unless `--approximate`; `COUPLING=STRUCTURAL` is written as the default coupling (reduced physics). |
| `*DISTRIBUTING COUPLING` | the `DCOUP2D` / `DCOUP3D` element is Abaqus' distributing constraint (Theory Guide): written as the same `*EQUATION`s, DOFs 1-6 (`DCOUP2D` 1, 2, 6) with the moments from the reference node's offset, weights from the data lines; the element leaves the mesh (ccx's card ties the translations alone). Kept as ccx's card (warned) with a `*MASS` on the element and under NLGEOM where the equations turn, unless `--approximate`. Proved by `validate_with_ccx.py` (`dcoup3d_verification`: the Abaqus Verification Guide's tables). |
| `*RIGID BODY` | `PIN NSET`/`TIE NSET` → `NSET` (both → their union); `REF NODE` set → node number; an explicit `ROT NODE` is added and BCs/moments on the reference point's DOFs 4-6 move to its DOFs 1-3 (ccx ignores them on the REF NODE); a reference point with a `*TRANSFORM` gives the `ROT NODE` its local axes (warned where they are undefined), in which connector constraints on it are written too. Shell/membrane/beam/truss members get knot beams; the rotations of `TIE NSET`/`ELSET` shell/beam members are tied to the `ROT NODE`, `PIN NSET` ones stay free. A body of rigid elements or an `ANALYTICAL SURFACE` becomes a `TIE NSET` of every node it moves (the skins', the rigid elements' own, rotary-inertia point masses, tied nodes); a plane or axisymmetric one is held out of its plane (reference node DOF 3, `ROT NODE` 1-2; repeated after `OP=NEW`). The data line (Abaqus/Explicit thickness) moves the skins' contact faces by half the thickness (`OFFSET` shifts them) and is not written; `DENSITY` with a thickness (rigid-element mass) leaves the elements unconverted unless `--approximate`; an analytical surface that is not meshed comments the body out. |
| `*PRE-TENSION SECTION` | `NODE` / `ELEMENT` set → its node / element number (Abaqus' set holds one; ccx 2.23 stops on a set name), also instance-qualified at the assembly level; any other set is warned and left for ccx to stop on. A truss or beam cut (`ELEMENT`) → `*EQUATION`s: the element ends at a copy of its last node, displaced from it by the pre-tension node's DOF 1 along the normal, with its rotations (ccx deletes the element instead, and stops on a truss or quadratic beam). |
| `*ROTARY INERTIA` | ccx 2.23 has no `ROTARYI` element: on a rigid body with a `*MASS`, the body's summed rotary inertia becomes six point masses on its principal axes around the body node with the largest mass, a negative `*MASS` there that takes their mass back, and four zero-density tetrahedra on those nodes (exact: same mass, centre of mass and inertia; in a plane model only I33, so the masses lie in the plane); an axisymmetric body's is dropped where the deck has no dynamic or frequency step, else only with `--approximate`; otherwise commented. In a part without `ORIENTATION` the tensor turns with its instance. |
| `*TRANSFORM` | rectangular and cylindrical cards passed through; `TYPE=S` (spherical — ccx has none and reads it as rectangular) commented out and replaced by a rectangular card per node with its spherical axes (1 radial, 3 meridional towards the pole, 2 = 3 × 1, fixed at the original position — exact); nodes on the polar axis keep the global axes (warned). Two cards with different data on a node (Abaqus does not allow it; ccx takes the last) and a 2-D node whose local 3-axis leaves Z (ccx 2.23 gets it wrong) are warned. BCs and moments on DOFs 4-6 of a transformed shell/beam node: kept where ccx reads them in the local axes (one local rotation on a beam node that is no knot, a shell node that is no knot), else in global components on a knot (beam nodes get a knot beam) where an exact form exists, else commented out. A corner node of S8 / S8R / S6 shells with translational BCs (ccx 2.23 ties them to its middle expanded node only), and a knot's in a deck where a `*DYNAMIC` step follows a linear step (ccx does not meet them there), leaves the card, its BCs and loads in global components where they have that form; else warned. |
| `*CLOAD` | moments on a rigid-body reference point → its `ROT NODE`; on a knotted shell/beam node or kinematic reference node with a `*TRANSFORM` → global components (see `*TRANSFORM`); `ORIENTATION=` (local axes) and `FOLLOWER=YES` dropped with a warning; `USER` commented, naming ccx's `cload.f`. |
| `*TEMPERATURE` | passed through (upgraded beams' midside nodes get their end nodes' mean); `USER` (Abaqus `UTEMP`) commented, naming ccx's `utemp.f`; in a `*BUCKLE` step commented (see `*BUCKLE`). |
| `*FILM / *DFLUX / *CFLUX / *RADIATE` | passed through, except loads from an Abaqus user subroutine (`USER`, a `...NU` label): commented, naming ccx's `film.f` / `dflux.f` / `cflux.f` / `radiate.f` (kept, ccx would run its stock subroutine instead). |
| `*DSFLUX / *SFILM / *SRADIATE` | → ccx's element-based `*DFLUX` / `*FILM` / `*RADIATE`: face `Sn` of the surface's solid or plane elements → label `Sn` / `Fn` / `Rn`, a blank value 0 (`validate_with_ccx.py surface_heat_loads_*`). Commented out where ccx would act differently: an `OP=NEW` with both card forms in the deck (Abaqus removes its own form only) or in a step with several cards, faces another card also loads (Abaqus adds them), shell faces, a `*FILM PROPERTY` table, `AVG` cavity radiation, `...NU` labels. |
| `*CONTACT PAIR` | missing `TYPE` → `NODE TO SURFACE` (the Abaqus/Standard default; the note suggests `SURFACE TO SURFACE` if ccx struggles to converge); `TIED` → `*TIE` (on a rigid master: its slave nodes join the rigid body; on membranes their nodes, see `*TIE`); `SMALL SLIDING` dropped for surface-to-surface; Abaqus-only params dropped. A line naming an analytical surface that is not meshed is commented out, the card's other lines kept. |
| `*SURFACE INTERACTION` | 2D out-of-plane thickness line dropped; `*SURFACE BEHAVIOR, PRESSURE-OVERCLOSURE=HARD` synthesized when missing (the Abaqus default). |
| `*FRICTION` | only `mu` emitted (ccx would read Abaqus' slip-rate / mu_k field as its stick slope); tables / exponential decay / anisotropy warned; `ROUGH` and `mu<=0` dropped. |
| `*PLASTIC` | `HARDENING=JOHNSON COOK` kept (ccx's native law) and given the `*RATE DEPENDENT, TYPE=JOHNSON COOK` card ccx needs to switch it on (C = 0 if the deck has none); `HARDENING=USER` and `DATATYPE=PARAMETERS` commented (ccx would silently skip them; reduced physics: ccx 2.23 has no user hardening, and its tabulated hardening cannot reproduce Chaboche back-stresses); `DEPENDENCIES` collapsed. |
| `*CYCLIC HARDENING` | kept in tabular form after a kept `*PLASTIC, HARDENING=COMBINED` of its material; the `PARAMETERS` form (Q_inf, b) is commented out (reduced physics), and so is a card without that `*PLASTIC` (an error in ccx). |
| `*NODAL THICKNESS / *NORMAL` | kept; a midside node the converter adds between two nodes that both have a value (an upgraded beam or shell) gets their interpolation (a normal: the normalised mean). |
| `*DAMAGE INITIATION` | ccx 2.23 evaluates `RICE TRACEY` and `JOHNSON COOK` only. `JOHNSON COOK` (d1-d5, melting and transition temperature, reference strain rate, as in Abaqus) is kept with the second data line ccx wants, the damage at which it deletes the element, set to `1E30` (a deletion can stop or crash 2.23): it then only reports the damage indicator (`DUCT`, to which Abaqus' `JCCRT` maps), as Abaqus does without a `*DAMAGE EVOLUTION` — where ccx reads it as meant: the deck's last `*MATERIAL` (ccx gives every card to it), plastic, all steps nonlinear `*STATIC`/`*DYNAMIC`, one card. Any other card is commented: exact without a `*DAMAGE EVOLUTION` (only the criterion output is lost), warned with one (the evolution is dropped anyway). |
| `*ELASTIC / *DENSITY / *SPECIFIC HEAT / *CONDUCTIVITY / *EXPANSION / *MOHR COULOMB / *MOHR COULOMB HARDENING` | `TYPE` token translated (`ORTHOTROPIC`→`ORTHO`, `ANISOTROPIC`→`ANISO`, same constant order); an isotropic `*ELASTIC` line with E alone gets ν = 0 (Abaqus' value for the blank field; ccx stops on the line); a cohesive `TYPE=TRACTION` in a material no section uses is commented (ccx would read it as E, ν); `DEPENDENCIES=n` (field variables, which ccx ignores) collapsed to the Abaqus no-field state, field = 0: the rows of that state, of the end of the table nearest 0 (which Abaqus holds beyond it), or interpolated between the two states around 0 when they share their temperatures — exact when the deck sets no field variable; otherwise reduced physics. A linear-elastic `*ELASTIC` less anisotropic than its material's `*EXPANSION` (isotropic beside `ORTHO`, isotropic / orthotropic / engineering constants beside `ANISO`) is written as `ENGINEERING CONSTANTS` / `ANISO` with the same stiffness, since ccx 2.23 otherwise uses a wrong stiffness in linear steps once the deck has temperatures; temperature rows are added so its stiffness interpolation stays within 1e-4 of Abaqus'. An `*EXPANSION, TYPE=ANISO` whose shear coefficients are zero in every row is written as `TYPE=ORTHO` (the elastic rule then follows `ORTHO`), since ccx 2.23 stops `NLGEOM` steps on any ANISO expansion once the deck has temperatures — unless an orientation or ply angle turns it so that it has shear in global axes. One with shear coefficients gets α12, α13, α23 halved on every row: Abaqus' are engineering (γ12 = α12 ΔT), ccx reads tensor components (ε12 = α12 ΔT). In a deck with a transient `*COUPLED TEMPERATURE-DISPLACEMENT` step the densities are divided and the specific heats multiplied by 10³⁰ (see there). |
| `*HYPERELASTIC` | no model keyword → `POLYNOMIAL` (Abaqus default); `TEST DATA INPUT` commented. |
| `*DEFORMATION PLASTICITY` | passed through. Reading it, ccx 2.23 runs the whole model under NLGEOM, the law in the logarithmic strain and the Cauchy stress, so a small-strain step (no `NLGEOM`) with it is reduced physics: Abaqus takes the small strain. An explicit `NLGEOM=NO` is dropped, as ccx then reads the small strain as a Green-Lagrange one. One that nothing uses is commented out. Its sections and plies name no orientation (see `*ORIENTATION`). |
| `*DEPVAR` | SDV count kept; label lines dropped; `DELETE=` warned (no element deletion in ccx; reduced physics). |
| `*USER MATERIAL` | kept, but the Abaqus subroutine does not run in a stock ccx: a mechanical one stops ccx ('no user material subroutine'; a name that would pick one of ccx's own routines gets `ABQ2CCX_` in front), a thermal one runs ccx's empty `umatht` (no conduction, no error). `--abaqus-umat` writes mechanical ones for ccx's Abaqus-UMAT interface, for a ccx rebuilt with the deck's UMAT. |
| `*INITIAL CONDITIONS` | `TYPE=STRESS/PLASTIC STRAIN/SOLUTION` expanded per integration point (SOLUTION continuation lines joined by the `*DEPVAR` size); stresses and plastic strains turned out of an orientation's axes, or a continuum shell's own, into the global ones ccx reads (at each integration point on a cylindrical or spherical system), in ccx's component order and shear measure; `REBAR` and `SECTION POINTS` records and unknown types commented. |
| `*CREEP` | Abaqus `LAW=STRAIN/TIME` → ccx Norton (default, time hardening — warned for strain hardening with m ≠ 0); other laws → `LAW=USER`. |
| `*AMPLITUDE` | keeps `NAME`/`TIME`/`SHIFTX`/`SHIFTY`; `SCALEX`/`SCALEY` applied to the data; `SMOOTH STEP` sampled, `EQUALLY SPACED` expanded, `PERIODIC` / `MODULATED` / `DECAY` sampled over the steps' time (200 points a period), `VALUE=ABSOLUTE` warned, `DEFINITION=USER` (Abaqus `UAMP`) commented, naming ccx's `uamplitude.f`. (`*AMP` alias accepted.) |
| `*RESTART` | keeps `WRITE`/`READ`/`FREQUENCY`/`STEP`; other params dropped. |
| `*SURFACE` | only `NAME`/`TYPE` kept; a line without a face label → its continuum elements' faces on the model's exterior, trimmed as Abaqus trims an open free surface (`TRIM`); shell edges `E1..E4` → `S3..S6` (plane elements `S1..S4`); `ANALYTICAL RIGID` / `COMBINE` commented; `SPOS`/`SNEG` kept (ccx reads them as the expanded shell's top and bottom face, as Abaqus); `CPS4I`/`CPE4I` edges `S1..S4` → `S3..S6` of their slabs; faces of rigid elements → the matching faces of their skins (no label: both sides); faces of surface elements (not in the ccx mesh) left out, a surface of them only dropped. `TYPE=SEGMENTS` / `CYLINDER` / `REVOLUTION` (analytical rigid surfaces) → skin facets of their rigid body, about the slave faces' size, named by an element-based surface of the same name: straight-line `SEGMENTS` and `CYLINDER` (over the model's extent along the generator) exactly; arcs (`CIRCL`, `PARAB`), `REVOLUTION` and `FILLET RADIUS` only under `--approximate` (`[APPROX]` with the chord angle and sag), otherwise commented with their body, pairs and ties. |
| `*OUTPUT / *NODE OUTPUT / *ELEMENT OUTPUT` | field output → `*NODE FILE`/`*EL FILE` (.frd), history output for a set → `*NODE PRINT`/`*EL PRINT` (.dat); the `*OUTPUT` card is dropped and its `FREQUENCY`/`NUMBER INTERVAL`/`TIME INTERVAL`/`TIME POINTS` go onto the step's first output card (ccx has one for all output of a step: the .frd requests' first, Abaqus' defaults kept; intervals → generated `*TIME POINTS`, or a frequency from a fixed or maximum increment, or in explicit dynamics from ccx's own stable increment, estimated with its Courant formula); `FREQUENCY=0` drops its requests. `VARIABLE=PRESELECT`/`ALL` → the ccx labels of Abaqus' preselected field output for the procedure (see output-reference), plus the variables named under it; preselected history output (energies) is dropped. A step without `*OUTPUT` requests of its own gets the field requests Abaqus carries over written again — at their own frequency, with its procedure's preselected variables, or Abaqus' preselected default where none carries over (ccx would keep the earlier step's cards and frequency); `OP=ADD`/`REPLACE` keeps them beside the step's own. Per .frd variable one node set (ccx keeps the last card's): the whole model before a set, several sets joined; a set the .frd cannot show — beam/shell nodes of a model ccx writes expanded, reference points — is also printed, or gets `OUTPUT=2D` when the deck's .frd output is only U/V/RF. |
| `*NODE FILE / *EL FILE / *NODE PRINT / *EL PRINT` | `POSITION=`/`DIRECTIONS=` stripped, `FREQ`→`FREQUENCY` (one per step, as above), `FREQUENCY=0` dropped, variables mapped and filtered against ccx's label list for that card (an unknown `*EL PRINT` label stops ccx); a print card without a set gets a whole-model set (Abaqus prints everything, ccx nothing). |
| `*CONTACT OUTPUT / *CONTACT FILE` | → `*CONTACT FILE`; `CDISP`/`CSTRESS` kept as ccx's `CDIS`/`CSTR`, other Abaqus contact variables dropped (a card left empty is dropped); `VARIABLE=PRESELECT`/`ALL` → the procedure's preselected contact output (none in linear perturbation steps; `PRESELECT` adds the variables named under it). Dropped too where the ccx model has no contact pair (general contact, a tied pair → `*TIE`), and where ccx 2.23 aborts on it: a model with axisymmetric elements whose `.frd` also gets `S`, unless every pair is `SURFACE TO SURFACE`. |
| `*CONTACT PRINT` | variables checked against ccx's list: `CSTRESS`/`CDISP` as `CSTR`/`CDIS`, `CFN`/`CFS`/`CFT` (→ `CF`) on one card per face-to-face pair the card covers, with its `SLAVE`/`MASTER` (ccx stops without them, segfaults on a node-to-surface pair); other variables and `NSET`/`SUMMARY`/`TOTALS` dropped; its `FREQUENCY` joins the step's output control. Dropped where the ccx model has no contact pair. |
| `Step data outside a *STEP` | `*CLOAD`, `*DLOAD`, output and procedure cards before the first step (or between steps) are commented — Abaqus rejects them, and ccx 2.23 segfaults when such a card ends the deck with a data line. |
| `INPUT= on data cards` | the referenced file's data lines are inlined (ccx reads `INPUT=` only on `*INCLUDE`). |
| `Load audit` | every step the Abaqus deck loads (loads, prescribed values, initial velocities; they persist across steps until `OP=NEW`) must still carry a load after conversion: a step whose loads were all commented out is warned (`Step N is loaded in the Abaqus deck ... but no load survives the conversion`), since ccx would solve it with no load; a deck that loads no step at all is noted. |

## Supported — emitted unchanged

CalculiX accepts these as-is (verified against the ccx 2.22 manual):

`*BASE MOTION`, `*CFD`, `*CHANGE CONTACT TYPE`, `*CHANGE FRICTION`, `*CHANGE MATERIAL`, `*CHANGE PLASTIC`, `*CHANGE SOLID SECTION`, `*CHANGE SURFACE BEHAVIOR`, `*CLEARANCE`, `*CONSTRAINT`, `*CONTACT DAMPING`, `*CONTROLS`, `*CORRELATION LENGTH`, `*CRACK PROPAGATION`, `*CYCLIC SYMMETRY MODEL`, `*DAMPING`, `*DESIGN RESPONSE`, `*DESIGN VARIABLES`, `*ELECTRICAL CONDUCTIVITY`, `*ELECTROMAGNETICS`, `*FACE PRINT`, `*FEASIBLE DIRECTION`, `*FLUID CONSTANTS`, `*FLUID SECTION`, `*GAP`, `*GAP CONDUCTANCE`, `*GAP HEAT GENERATION`, `*GEOMETRIC CONSTRAINT`, `*GEOMETRIC TOLERANCES`, `*GREEN`, `*HCF`, `*HEADING`, `*INCLUDE`, `*INITIAL MESH`, `*INITIAL STRAIN INCREASE`, `*MAGNETIC PERMEABILITY`, `*MASS FLOW`, `*MATERIAL`, `*MATRIX ASSEMBLE`, `*MODAL DAMPING`, `*MODAL DYNAMIC`, `*MODEL CHANGE`, `*NETWORK MPC`, `*NO ANALYSIS`, `*OBJECTIVE`, `*PHYSICAL CONSTANTS`, `*RATE DEPENDENT`, `*REFINE MESH`, `*RETAINED NODAL DOFS`, `*ROBUST DESIGN`, `*SECTION PRINT`, `*SELECT CYCLIC SYMMETRY MODES`, `*SENSITIVITY`, `*SPECIFIC GAS CONSTANT`, `*STEADY STATE DYNAMICS`, `*SUBMODEL`, `*SUBSTRUCTURE GENERATE`, `*SUBSTRUCTURE MATRIX OUTPUT`, `*SURFACE BEHAVIOR`, `*TIME POINTS`, `*UNCOUPLED TEMPERATURE-DISPLACEMENT`, `*USER SECTION`, `*VALUES AT INFINITY`, `*VIEWFACTOR`

## Passed through with a heads-up

| Keyword | Note |
| --- | --- |
| `*USER ELEMENT` | *USER ELEMENT kept; ensure the matching ccx user-element routine is built in. |

## Same name, different meaning (warned)

| Keyword | Warning |
| --- | --- |
| `*FILTER` | *FILTER in CalculiX is a sensitivity-smoothing card for *SENSITIVITY steps, NOT the Abaqus output filter — emitted as-is but almost certainly wrong; remove it unless this is an optimisation run. |

## Dropped — organisational, no ccx meaning

Silently dropped (with a note): `*ASSEMBLY`, `*END ASSEMBLY`, `*END INSTANCE`, `*END LOAD CASE`, `*END PART`, `*INSTANCE`, `*MANIFEST`, `*PART`, `*PREPRINT`.

Dropped with a warning (can change the model):

| Keyword | Warning |
| --- | --- |
| `*SYSTEM` | *SYSTEM (local coordinate system for following *NODE cards) is unsupported by ccx and was dropped; node coordinates defined under it may be in a rotated frame — verify they are global. |
| `*UNIT SYSTEM` | *UNIT SYSTEM is unsupported by ccx and was dropped (informational only). |

## Output requests and numerical controls without a ccx card — commented out, a note

They do not change the model ccx solves. Output and diagnostics requests: `*CONTOUR INTEGRAL`, `*DIAGNOSTICS`, `*ELEMENT MATRIX OUTPUT`, `*ELEMENT RESPONSE`, `*ENERGY FILE`, `*ENERGY OUTPUT`, `*ENERGY PRINT`, `*FILE FORMAT`, `*FILE OUTPUT`, `*INCREMENTATION OUTPUT`, `*INTEGRATED OUTPUT`, `*INTEGRATED OUTPUT SECTION`, `*MODAL FILE`, `*MODAL OUTPUT`, `*MODAL PRINT`, `*MONITOR`, `*NODE RESPONSE`, `*PRINT`, `*RADIATION FILE`, `*RADIATION OUTPUT`, `*RADIATION PRINT`, `*SECTION FILE`, `*SURFACE PRINT`, `*USER OUTPUT VARIABLES`.

| Numerical control | Note |
| --- | --- |
| `*BULK VISCOSITY` | Abaqus/Explicit's artificial bulk viscosity (it damps the solution numerically); ccx's explicit solver has none |
| `*SOLUTION TECHNIQUE` | the Newton / quasi-Newton choice; ccx uses its own |
| `*SOLVER CONTROLS` | iterative solver settings; ccx uses its own |
| `*CONTACT CONTROLS` | contact algorithm settings; ccx uses its own |

## No CalculiX equivalent — commented out with guidance

Any other keyword not in the CalculiX set and without a translator is emitted as `**` comments plus a warning, and recorded as reduced physics (`Converter.reduced_physics`): ccx then solves the model without it. These have tailored guidance:

| Keyword | Guidance |
| --- | --- |
| `*VISCOELASTIC` | time-domain viscoelasticity is unsupported (ccx *VISCO is a creep STEP, not a material); drop, or approximate with *DAMPING. |
| `*INERTIA RELIEF` | ccx has no inertia relief; constrain with a soft spring-to-ground / 3-2-1 set, or balance with the equilibrating load. |
| `*CONNECTOR BEHAVIOR` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a section that uses it is commented out); remodel as *SPRING / *DASHPOT / *MPC per the behaviour. |
| `*CONNECTOR MOTION` | prescribes motion of connector components, which the converted connector (ccx constraints, no connector element) does not have; the prescribed motion is missing. |
| `*CONNECTOR LOAD` | loads connector components, which the converted connector (ccx constraints, no connector element) does not have; the load is missing. |
| `*GASKET BEHAVIOR` | gasket behaviour has no ccx equivalent. |
| `*DAMAGE EVOLUTION` | ccx 2.23 added *DAMAGE INITIATION but not *DAMAGE EVOLUTION, so progressive damage cannot fully run (the material will not soften/fail); drop. |
| `*FIELD` | *FIELD predefined fields are unsupported; use *INITIAL CONDITIONS / *TEMPERATURE / *DISTRIBUTION instead. |
| `*REBAR` | rebar/reinforcement layers have no ccx equivalent; mesh reinforcements explicitly. |
| `*CONCRETE` | concrete plasticity models are unsupported by ccx; substitute *PLASTIC or remodel. |
| `*CONCRETE DAMAGED PLASTICITY` | unsupported by ccx; substitute *PLASTIC or remodel. |
| `*CONNECTOR ELASTICITY` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR DAMPING` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR STOP` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR LOCK` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR FRICTION` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR PLASTICITY` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR HARDENING` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR DAMAGE INITIATION` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR DAMAGE EVOLUTION` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR CONSTITUTIVE REFERENCE` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR DERIVED COMPONENT` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR POTENTIAL` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR UNIAXIAL BEHAVIOR` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR FAILURE` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONTACT` | Abaqus general contact has no ccx equivalent; define explicit pairs instead: *CONTACT PAIR, INTERACTION=<name>, TYPE=SURFACE TO SURFACE with two element surfaces (+ *SURFACE INTERACTION / *SURFACE BEHAVIOR). |
| `*CONTACT INCLUSIONS` | general-contact inclusion list (ALL EXTERIOR is not translatable); create the two surfaces and a *CONTACT PAIR instead. |
| `*CONTACT EXCLUSIONS` | general-contact exclusion list; not applicable to ccx *CONTACT PAIR. |
| `*CONTACT PROPERTY ASSIGNMENT` | assigns a general-contact property; in ccx name the *SURFACE INTERACTION via *CONTACT PAIR, INTERACTION= instead. |
| `*LATENT HEAT` | ccx has no *LATENT HEAT; approximate with an apparent *SPECIFIC HEAT peak cp + L/(Tliq-Tsol) over the melting interval. |
| `*EMBEDDED ELEMENT` | no ccx equivalent; mesh the reinforcement conformally or tie the embedded nodes with *EQUATION constraints. |
| `*ALLOWABLE STRESS` | Abaqus 2024 optimisation stress limit; ccx has no equivalent — express a stress constraint via *DESIGN RESPONSE/*CONSTRAINT in a *SENSITIVITY run. |
| `*REDUCED BASIS GENERATE` | Abaqus 2024 reduced-order-basis generation has no ccx equivalent; drop. |
| `*SUBMODEL CUT` | Abaqus 2024 submodel-cut card; ccx drives submodels with *SUBMODEL plus *BOUNDARY/*CLOAD, SUBMODEL — remodel using those. |
| `*WEAR SURFACE PROPERTIES` | Abaqus 2024 surface-wear properties have no ccx equivalent; drop. |
| `*ELECTRICAL RESISTIVITY` | ccx parameterises conduction by *ELECTRICAL CONDUCTIVITY (the inverse); convert resistivity -> conductivity. |
| `*ELECTRIC MACHINE LOAD` | Abaqus 2024 electric-machine load has no ccx equivalent; drop. |
| `*ELECTRIC MACHINE PROPERTY` | Abaqus 2024 electric-machine property has no ccx equivalent; drop. |
| `*ELEMENT USER OUTPUT VARIABLES` | Abaqus UVARM-style user output; ccx has no equivalent (fill state variables via *DEPVAR + a ccx umat instead). |
| `*PIEZORESISTIVITY` | Abaqus 2024 piezoresistive coupling has no ccx equivalent; drop. |
| `*STEP CYCLING` | Abaqus 2025 step cycling has no ccx equivalent; remodel as repeated steps. |
| `*STEP CYCLING CONTROL` | Abaqus 2025 step-cycling controls have no ccx equivalent; drop. |
| `*LOAD CASE` | Abaqus allows load cases only in a linear perturbation *STATIC or *STEADY STATE DYNAMICS step, and ccx solves one load case per step: the loads of all *LOAD CASE blocks in this step are SUPERPOSED into one solution. |
